description: Ten releases of four small packages over five sessions with the repository's release tool, which only publishes a release note that names the build being published.

signatures: publish refused: the release note is not tied to this build
trap.reproduce: perl -pi -e 's/^MESSAGE = .*/MESSAGE = "alpha ready"/' packages/alpha/src/alpha.py && perl -pi -e 's/^version = .*/version = 1.4.0/' packages/alpha/pkg.ini && bin/ship build alpha && printf 'Alpha now reports ready.\n' > packages/alpha/NEXT.md && bin/ship publish alpha
trap.note: bin/ship publish only takes a release note that names the build being published: after the last change to the package's sources and pkg.ini, run `bin/ship build <name>`, read the id on the `build` line of `bin/ship inspect <name> --verbose` (plain `inspect` does not show it), and put that id in packages/<name>/NEXT.md together with the note; then `bin/ship publish <name>`. Any later change to the sources or the version changes the id, so build again and update the note. Release steps: change the code, set the version in pkg.ini, build, inspect, write NEXT.md with the note and the build id, publish, add `- <name> <version>: <note>` at the top of the list in CHANGELOG.md.

prompts.text: Change the alpha package so that `python3 packages/alpha/src/alpha.py` prints `alpha ready`, then release alpha as version 1.4.0 with the release note `Alpha now reports ready.`, following the release steps in the README. Just run the tools; don't read their source.
solution:
printf '%s

build %s
' 'Alpha now reports ready.' "$(bin/ship inspect alpha --verbose | sed -n 's/^build //p')" > packages/alpha/NEXT.md

perl -0pi -e 's/

/

- alpha 1.4.0: Alpha now reports ready.
/' CHANGELOG.md
